Minor spec bumps and a new paint job - along with minuscule performance differences - are all that separate Super and non-Super. So it's all about value. Is a $200 price-cut good enough? And is there a threshold point for ultra high-end 4K gaming - and if so, do the RTX 4080 and 4080 Super meet it?

comments.text:
Anyone complaining about the price of the 4080(super) I GET YA, I'm also not about to blow $1000+ on a GPU (which is fine because between the 6700XT all the way through the 4070ti super, we have some GREAT 1440p-4k GPUs at GREAT prices right now) but with that being said, How much VRAM did the 3080 have? How much does it cost to use the same VRAM, but tuned to a higher speed? How big is the cooler on the 3080 in comparison to a 4080? How much lower of a quality was the silicon used in the 3080 as opposed to the 4080? Speaking of silicon, how much is the going price for higher quality silicon than in the days of the prior 80 series cards? On top of all of that (and more that I can't think of ATM) we have inflation. 

Do I think $1000 is too much? Yes, but I'm also not an expert on GPUs and while I believe the price increase is justified to a degree, I don't know how much of a degree, but I DO know that somewhat of a price increase is justified for sure. The products cost more to manufacture than they used to. 

That being said, I wasn't actively paying attention to the MSRP of graphics cards during the pandemic, as I've always been a used hardware kind of guy. I just got a 3080 for $300 because it has a custom AIO cooling solution and nobody else wanted it. I jumped on that to replace an alienware RX 6800XT I had that started to die (which was my fault for buying an alienware version of that card that is basically a glorified reference card with the same exact PCB and probably an inferior cooler on it to try and save a few bucks) 
It also seems like a major jump in performance, going from the 3080 to the 4080, but so was the 2080 to the 3080. I know that firsthand because I upgraded from a 2080 super (also with an AIO lol this one was the "EVGA 2080 super hybrid" and not a custom job like my 3080) to the 6800XT (which is pretty much the same as a 3080 in average frame rate) and then to the 3080 a few months later after the 6800xt started artifacting and overheating, and before that I had a 1080 (non ti) and the jump from the 1080 to the 2080 super was extremely lackluster, so lackluster in fact that I was wishing I had gone with a 1080ti instead of a 2080 super (same performance, but the 2080 super has less VRAM) and then I came into a 1440p display and that's what caused me to keep GPU hopping as the 8GB VRAM just wasn't enough, and I wanted something that was all around powerful, not just extra VRAM as I pretty much exclusively play AAA games, and I'm a sucker for higher frame rates than usual in those games. For example, I like to play RDR2 at 100+ FPS 1440p for no reason when 60 fps would absolutely suffice, and I use a controller so while nonsensical, I just like higher frame rates, but I'm not a snob (unless your someone who considers someone who will not play at frame rates below 45 a snob) and will absolutely play at 60 FPS, or even 45 FPS If I have to. Never 30 though, as I would rather just not play the game at that point.
